description:
FILED s462at (agent AT, round 19), found by the #940 probe family and then
isolated on its own.  PRE-EXISTING and unrelated to #940's parse: the parse is
now right, and this is what the correctly-parsed program then answers.

perl: a FAILED m// with NO capture groups returns the EMPTY LIST in list
context (and the defined-false "" in scalar context).  PCL returns a
one-element false value in BOTH.  Probed 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl:

    $_ = "zzz"; my @r = (/q+/, "four");
        perl  @r == 1,  ("four")
        PCL   @r == 2,  ("", "four")

    sub f { print scalar(@_) } $_ = "zzz"; f(/q+/, "x");
        perl  1
        PCL   2

    $_ = "zzz"; my $r = /q+/;                    BOTH ""        (scalar ctx ok)
    my @r = ("abc" =~ /(q)(q)/);  print @r+0;    BOTH 0         (WITH captures ok)
    my @r = ("abc" =~ /(a)(b)/);  print "@r";    BOTH "a b"     (success ok)
    $_ = "zzz"; my @r = (/z+/, "four");          BOTH 2         (success ok)

So the CAPTURE-BEARING path already returns () on failure; only the
capture-LESS one manufactures an element.  perl's rule is uniform: a failed
match yields () in list context whatever the pattern.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND A COUNT: this shape is a Test::More idiom.
`ok /pat/, "desc"` passes the match INTO a list operator, so on failure perl
hands the sub ("desc") and PCL hands it ("", "desc") -- the arguments SHIFT BY
ONE and the row reads its description as its verdict.  That is how it was
found: three of the #940 probe rows print `not ok - four` where perl prints
`ok - ` (perl's $_[0] is the DESCRIPTION, a true string).

WHERE: cl/pcl-runtime.lisp's `do-regex-match'.  The m// path already knows
whether it is in list context (*wantarray*) and already returns the capture
LIST there; the miss is the no-capture branch, which returns the scalar answer
in both contexts.  Task #416 is the neighbouring rule that must not move: a
failed match's SCALAR answer is the dualvar ("" , 0), not 0 -- keep that, and
change only the LIST-context value to the empty list.

BAR: the six rows above vs perl; the #416 rows unmoved; the #940 rows in
Pl/t/transpile-test-10.t extended with the `q+`/`qq*`/`tr*` spellings, which
are exactly the three that still disagree there today and would then agree;
full sweep (every m// goes through this).

=== SHIPPED s463au (agent AU, round 20), together with #459 â same bug, two
=== task numbers, one fix.  Both CLOSED.

WHAT SHIPPED.  `do-regex-match`'s no-match arm returns `(%p-empty-list)` in
list context instead of raw NIL.  `%p-empty-list` is a new one-line function
returning a fresh zero-length adjustable vector, and it is now THE ONE
producer of Perl's empty list as a runtime value: `%pcl-no-op-import-result`
(#534) and `p-return-value`'s list-context nil arm spelled the same
`(make-array 0 :adjustable t :fill-pointer 0)` and were routed through it
(rule 11 â #534's own docstring already called it "the same shape every other
empty-list producer yields").

WHY RAW NIL WAS WRONG, precisely: raw nil is the runtime's empty list to
EXACTLY ONE consumer, %p-flatten-list, which drops it as an empty-list/hole
marker.  p-array-fill's %p-array-fill-item KEEPS it (as an array HOLE, by
design) and p-flatten-args SPREADS it as one argument.  So the sole-RHS
spelling `my @l = (/zzz/)` was right and everything else was one element long.

THE TASK TEXT WAS WRONG ON ONE POINT, and the measurement is the record: #962
says the capture-BEARING path already returned () on failure.  It did not â
`(/(z)(z)/, "b")` was 2 elements too.  The arm is shared; only the sole-RHS
spelling hid it.  The /g LIST arm WAS already right (it builds a vector), and
that is what identified the fix's shape.

#416 IS THE NEIGHBOUR AND IT DID NOT MOVE: a failed match's SCALAR answer is
still the defined-false "", s/// still "", tr/// still the count 0.

BARS MET.  Runtime-only: emission untouched, so no corpus-diff, no generation
bump, no artifact rebuild.
  * 40-row probe battery vs perl 5.40.3, 39 identical.  The 40th is
    `printf("%s|%s\n", /zzz/, "b", "c")`: p-printf's ARGUMENT LIST is not
    evaluated in list context while p-print's is, so the match ran in scalar
    context and answered "".  PRE-EXISTING and unrelated (verified on the base
    tree, where print/sprintf/join were wrong too and now are right).  Filed
    as #970.
  * FULL SWEEP: GATE clean, TOTAL passing 18343 -> 18343 (+0), 0 new / 0
    fixed, drops 5 = census.
  * Companion `--dir re --dir op --quick`: see the session log.
  * Guards: `Pl/t/match-vars-01.t` 34 -> 39 (argument arity, the
    `ok /pat/, "desc"` inversion, every list consumer, the #416 INVERSE row,
    the count/boolean/return consumers), inverse-verified on 6e6f191;
    `Pl/t/transpile-test-10.t`'s #940 row extended with the `q+`/`qq*`/`tr*`
    spellings the task named.
  * `docs/ir-spec.md`: the regex row states the two-context contract; the
    empty-list note names the one producer.
subject: a FAILED capture-less m// returns a false ELEMENT in list context where perl returns the EMPTY LIST -- shifts every argument of `ok /pat/, "desc"'
